cohort: The study included patients admitted to hospitals in the United States for either a heart attack or childbirth, drawn from a nationally representative dataset of inpatient hospital admissions.
finding: Being uninsured had no effect on the probability of bypass surgery for heart attack patients, but it was associated with a substantially lower probability of a C-section delivery for patients admitted for childbirth.
mod_finding: Uninsured patients admitted for childbirth had a substantially lower probability of a C-section delivery.
